newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Finnish president talks trade in Brazil.
newsitem.headline: Finnish president talks trade in Brazil.

text.p: Finnish President Martti Ahtisaari met his Brazilian counterpart Fernando Henrique Cardoso on Monday for talks on economic and political ties, officials said.

Ahtisaari, on a week-long visit to Latin America's largest country, told reporters that boosting exports was one of his principal aims and that a high-level business delegation travelling with him was exploring investment opportunities.
"This visit demonstrates that Finland's interests do not just lie in Europe now that we have joined the European Union," the Finnish president said through an interpreter.
He singled out forestry, telecommunications, mining, metals and agriculture as sectors Finnish companies want to invest in.

Ole Norrback, minister for Europe and for foreign trade, said economic ties would be boosted by an accord signed last year between the European Union and the four-nation Mercosur trade bloc grouping Brazil, Argentina, Uruguay and Paraguay.
The deal prepares the way for talks on an eventual free trade agreement between the two regional entities.
"There are still some obstacles to be overcome but I think that by the year 2000, trade between us will be very much more free," Norrback said.
The Finnish president and his delegation were due to travel to Brazil's industrial heartland of Sao Paulo on Tuesday.
Ahtisaari was scheduled to spend next weekend at the spectacular Iguacu falls before flying on to Argentina.
